text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet calls for restrained increase in nominal income to preserve price stability and competitiveness, public deficit cuts.
-- Thomson-CSF does not favour vertical alliance with Aerospatiale because that would not open new markets, according to a Defence Ministry source.
-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to name a council of economic advisers.
-- France Telecom interested in buying cable networks from Generale des Eaux, in which Canal Plus and Time Warner may also be interested.
LA TRIBUNE

-- Prime Minister Jospin, in a letter to the experts carrying out public finances audit, says he is watching public deficits closely, but does not commit himself to bringing deficit to three percent of GDP in 1998.
-- Retail group Pinault-Printemps-Redoute to diversify in telecommunications equipment, sporting goods sectors.
-- Canal Plus pay TV company to pull out of the German market to strengthen its position in Italy.
-- Paris bourse nears record volume with 17 billion francs of turnover on Tuesday.
L'AGEFI
-- Dassault Aviation expects higher sales, target for 1997 and 1998 is for sales between 15 and 20 billion francs.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Government will finance first policy measures by decree this summer, will wait until end of the year to present mini-budget, according to Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn.
-- Bank of France governor Trichet calls for lower state-controlled interest levels on savings.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- European Commission reaffirms need to respect Maastricht treaty criteria on public deficits.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Finance Minister Strauss-Kahn says government may reduce some spending commitments if public deficits turn out higher than expected.
